title: Cohomology and joint detection by system evaluations
statement:
For strict systems over any ring-sheaf sequence B, derived evaluation commutes naturally with every homology functor. A derived system morphism is invertible exactly when all evaluated morphisms are invertible. A derived system has a fixed lower or upper cohomological bound exactly when all its evaluations have that same bound. A cochain-system map is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when each component is.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
theorem systemDerivedEvaluation_bounds_iff
    (M : DerivedCategory (StrictRingSystem B)) (q : ℤ) :
    (M.IsGE q ↔ ∀ n, ((derivedSystemEvaluation B n).obj M).IsGE q) ∧
      (M.IsLE q ↔ ∀ n, ((derivedSystemEvaluation B n).obj M).IsLE q)
```

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21, ordinary evaluation left extension and the subsequence generalization; Stacks 03DA, 03DB, 06YT and 07D9

proof.text: Apply exact functor compatibility with homology. A strict system is zero exactly when each component is zero, so componentwise homology detects acyclicity and each cohomological bound. In an abelian derived category the cone criterion and homology detection characterize isomorphisms. Finally quasi-isomorphisms are exactly the maps inverted by Q, and the exact evaluation factorizations transfer this criterion to components.
